# Charlotta

## Overview

- **Age:** Teenager (fourteen in volume 2, sixteen or seventeen in volume 3)  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- **Role:** Handmaiden / Maidservant  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Charlotta the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a heavily freckled face with a snub nose, plump figure, and a very wide mouth and smile. In her earlier teens, she wore her hair in many braids fastened with large, bright blue ribbon bows. Upon reaching young ladyhood, she discarded her blue bows and began wearing her hair in an enormous pompadour.

_Sources: [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P47](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0047), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c28 P72](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0072), [v2 c30 P27](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0027), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007)_

## Personality

Charlotta is fiercely devoted and loyal to her mistress, Miss Lavendar, whom she adores. She is energetic, brisk, and practical, though she is easily anxious about potential mishaps. She enthusiastically admires Anne Shirley and attempts to copy her manners and movements. Despite her pragmatic nature, she is agreeable to imaginative ideas and loves a good romance.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055), [v2 c28 P65](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0065), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v2 c30 P14](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0014)_

## History

Charlotta the Fourth went to live at Echo Lodge as a young teenager to serve as a handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis. She quickly formed a deep attachment to her mistress, keeping her company and indulging her imaginative pretense without judgment. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them warmly and was thrilled by Anne's grace, continually practicing in front of a mirror to mimic Anne's mannerisms. She worried greatly over Miss Lavendar's mood and health, confiding her fears to Anne. When Stephen Irving returned to propose to Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was intensely excited, helping Anne manage the household and watching over the romance. She eagerly assisted with the wedding preparations and served at the outdoor ceremony in late August. Following the wedding, Charlotta moved to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving and Paul, though she felt terribly homesick at first. She returned to Echo Lodge with the family during subsequent summer vacations, having grown into a young lady.

## Background by volume

- Her real name is Leonora, given by her mother Mrs. Bowman who liked fancy names  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- She is the youngest of the Bowman girls, following her sisters Charlotta, Julietta, and Evelina  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Her mistress dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth' to avoid confusing her with her older sisters who previously worked at Echo Lodge  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Came to stay with Miss Lavendar at age fourteen for board and clothes  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

> They're not things that go by habit. They just happen . . . and there you are. Anybody can have a stroke.  <sub>[v2 c30 P16](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0016)</sub>

> A wedding ain't much cheerfuller than a funeral after all, when it's all over, Miss Shirley, ma'am.  <sub>[v2 c30 P35](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0035)</sub>

> You don't think I talk with a Yankee accent, do you, Miss Shirley, ma'am?  <sub>[v3 c23 P8](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0008)</sub>

> When all's said and done, Miss Shirley, ma'am, I haven't seen any one in Boston that's equal to you  <sub>[v3 c40 P1](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0001)</sub>
